title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 18
paragraphs: Having parted, both sides gladly made for their moorings; and after they had separated and left the sea-fight — although the Greeks held possession of the bodies of the dead and of the wreckage — they had suffered severely (especially the Athenians, half of whose ships had been disabled), and so they were now deliberating about retreating to the inner parts of Greece.
